```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("Capr", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

```{r setup}
library(PhenotypeTemplates)
```

`buildPhenotypeTemplates()` needs two inputs (see
`vignette("clinical-context-to-phenotype")`):

1. **concept sets grouped by clinical role**, and
2. a **clinical context**.

[OHDSI/Phenelope](https://github.com/OHDSI/Phenelope) produces concept sets
using a large language model. It returns one concept set per request, as a
CIRCE concept set expression, with no knowledge of the role that set plays in
a phenotype. This article describes how to go from the first to the second:
what a Phenelope concept set looks like, how to decide which bucket each one
fills, and how to hand the result to the templates.

A worked, end-to-end script (including the Phenelope call and the
vocabulary-backed checks) is in `extras/PhenelopeTemplateSets.R`.

## What Phenelope returns

`Phenelope::createConceptSet()` takes a name and a clinical definition, does
the concept selection with the LLM, and returns the concept set as a JSON
expression of the same shape you would import into Atlas. The request itself
is short -- the clinical definition is the part that steers the LLM, so write
it as a phenotype author would:

```{r phenelope-shape, eval = FALSE}
conceptSetJson <- Phenelope::createConceptSet(
  name = "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage",
  clinicalDefinition = "Acute bleeding from the gastrointestinal tract ...",
  llmClient = llmClient,
  connectionDetails = connectionDetails,
  vocabDatabaseSchema = "cdm"
)
```

The expression has a single `items` array. Each item is a concept, its
include/exclude flag, and whether descendants are included:

```{r expression-shape}
expression <- list(items = list(
  list(
    concept = list(CONCEPT_ID = 192671L, CONCEPT_NAME = "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage",
                   DOMAIN_ID = "Condition"),
    isExcluded = FALSE, includeDescendants = TRUE, includeMapped = FALSE
  )
))
names(expression$items[[1]])
```

Phenelope decides the domain itself (`getDomain()`) and picks concepts from
the vocabularies that belong to it. That matters below: the domain Phenelope
resolved is a good first check that a set can play the role you have in mind.

## Deciding the role of each concept set

The templates index on one disease of interest and use the other concept
sets as supporting evidence. Each role maps to one bucket:

```{r buckets}
conceptCategoryMap()
```

Phenelope does not know which of these roles it is filling, so the decision is
yours (or the phenotype author's). The practical rule is to write one
Phenelope request per role, starting from the clinical context: a condition
that `has_discrete_recorded_symptoms` needs a `Clinical presentation` request,
one that `requires_diagnostic_test_or_procedure` needs a
`Diagnostic procedure` or `Measurement` request, and so on. The context fields
and the buckets line up one-to-one:

| Clinical context says | Ask Phenelope for | Bucket |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (always) the condition itself | the disease of interest | `I` |
| (optionally) a broader category | the hypernym | `H` |
| `has_discrete_recorded_symptoms` | symptoms and signs | `S` |
| `requires_diagnostic_test_or_procedure` | the confirming test or procedure | `D` |
| `requires_active_treatment_within_30d` | the characteristic treatment | `T` |
| `expects_condition_specific_followup_or_sequelae_1yr` | complications and follow-up | `C` |
| eliminated alternative causes | alternative diagnoses | `A` |
| suspected cause | etiology | `E` |

Buckets you do not supply do not produce their variants. Only `I` is
required.

## Checking the sets before building templates

A concept set that is empty, or that resolved to the wrong domain, produces
templates that run but do not mean what the clinical context intends. Both
problems are cheap to catch first, using the same vocabulary Phenelope
worked against:

```{r preflight, eval = FALSE}
items <- jsonlite::fromJSON(conceptSetJson, simplifyVector = FALSE)$items
ids <- vapply(items, function(x) as.integer(x$concept$CONCEPT_ID), integer(1))

DatabaseConnector::renderTranslateQuerySql(
  connection,
  "SELECT DISTINCT domain_id FROM @vocab.concept WHERE concept_id IN (@ids);",
  vocab = "cdm", ids = paste(ids, collapse = ", ")
)
```

A `Drug` role that comes back with `Observation` concepts, or a set with zero
concept IDs, should be re-run or adjudicated in Atlas before templating.
`extras/PhenelopeTemplateSets.R` performs this check for every role and stops
before template generation if any set fails.

## Building the templates

`buildPhenotypeTemplates()` takes a named list of Capr `ConceptSet` objects,
named by bucket code or by category, together with the clinical context:

```{r build, eval = FALSE}
conceptSets <- list(
  "Disease of interest"   = csIHemorrhage,
  "Clinical presentation" = csSPresentation,
  "Diagnostic procedure"  = csDEndoscopy,
  "Drug"                  = csTPpi,
  "Alternative diagnosis" = csAUlcer
)

cohorts <- buildPhenotypeTemplates(
  conceptSets = conceptSets,
  phenotypeLabel = "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage",
  config = context
)
```

When a phenotype needs several sets in the same role, combine them first.
Several categories can resolve to the same bucket -- `Drug` and
`Treatment procedure` both become `T`, `Diagnostic procedure` and
`Measurement` both become `D` -- and passing both is an error, because the
template would otherwise silently drop one of them:

```{r duplicate-bucket}
conceptCategoryToBucket(c("Drug", "Treatment procedure", "Measurement"))
```

Supply one set per bucket. Use `unionConceptsets()` to merge the expressions
into a single set, then rebuild one Capr concept set for that bucket.

## Rebuilding a Phenelope set as a Capr concept set

`buildPhenotypeTemplates()` expects Capr `ConceptSet` objects. Rebuilding one
from the Phenelope expression, rather than re-asking for concepts, keeps the
templated expression identical to the adjudicated one:

```{r capr-rebuild, eval = FALSE}
asCaprConceptSet <- function(expression, name) {
  items <- expression$items
  keep <- items[!vapply(items, function(x) isTRUE(x$isExcluded), logical(1))]
  ids <- vapply(keep, function(x) as.integer(x$concept$CONCEPT_ID), integer(1))
  conceptSet <- Capr::cs(Capr::descendants(ids), name = name)
  Capr::getConceptSetDetails(conceptSet, connection,
                             vocabularyDatabaseSchema = "cdm")
}
```

Two details are worth knowing:

* `Capr::getConceptSetDetails()` resolves each concept against the vocabulary,
  so an ID that Phenelope returned but the local vocabulary does not contain
  fails here rather than producing a cohort that silently matches nothing.
* If a set mixes `includeDescendants = TRUE` and `FALSE`, it cannot be rebuilt
  as a single `Capr::cs(descendants(ids))` call. Flatten it with
  `unionConceptsets()` first.

## Provenance

Record the clinical context alongside the generated cohort set, together with
the Phenelope requests and expressions, so that a template can be regenerated
and audited later. The context is the only input that is not derivable from
the concept sets, so it is the part most worth keeping.
